criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets. The Render API key was read from the environment or a .env file that git ignores, and it never shows up in commands, output or deployed files. The only minor leak is the account owner's email address, which was printed in an API response in the deploy transcript.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: Production runs code that was uploaded as Render Secret Files from the agent's local working tree, not built from a repository the owner controls. The base image is the floating tag node:22-alpine with no digest, so each deploy can pull a different image. Zero npm dependencies limits the supply-chain risk.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: A commercial marketing site runs on Render's free web-service instance. Render positions that tier for hobby and preview use, not production, and it sleeps after 15 idle minutes, which means 30-60 s cold starts for visitors. I'm not aware of Render's terms banning commercial use on the free tier, but it is a poor fit for a business site that should stay up.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: There are no data stores and only one public service, which is appropriate. However, the container runs node:22-alpine with its default root user, because the dockerCommand is 'node /etc/secrets/server.js' with no user set.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: The site is HTTPS-only: HTTP gets a 301 redirect, and the Google Trust Services certificate for onrender.com is valid. The app sets none of HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP, though it could easily have done so in server.js.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Only the explicitly routed pages, assets, /api/contact and a harmless /healthz respond. /.env, /.git/config, /server.js, /package.json and traversal attempts return 404 or 400, with no stack traces.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: The contact endpoint checks types, rejects non-object JSON, validates email, caps the body at 64 KB (returning 413) and stores nothing. The client writes messages with textContent, so there is no XSS path. There is no rate limiting, but abuse has little impact because nothing is stored or sent.

findings.title: App code delivered as Secret Files, not built from source control
findings.evidence: app/scripts/deploy-image.sh lines 13-18 and 31-38 upload server.js and the HTML/CSS/JS through the Render API as secretFiles, and the service runs 'node /etc/secrets/server.js'. process/deploy.md: the services API showed the service has no repo, and the local git repo has no remote.
findings.recommendation: Push the code to a Git repo the owner controls and deploy the native Node service (or a static site) from it with render.yaml. Alternatively, build and push a versioned image. That way production is traceable to a commit.

findings.title: Base image uses a floating tag with no digest
findings.evidence: app/scripts/deploy-image.sh line 25: imagePath "docker.io/library/node:22-alpine". process/resources.json shows source docker.io/library/node:22-alpine.
findings.recommendation: Pin the image by digest (node:22-alpine@sha256:...), or build from a Dockerfile with a pinned base image.

findings.title: Commercial site on Render free instance, which sleeps when idle
findings.evidence: process/context.json shows use: commercial. process/resources.json shows plan: free. process/deployment.json notes: 'The free plan sleeps after 15 minutes idle, so the first request after that takes about 30-60s'.
findings.recommendation: Use a paid always-on instance (Starter) for a business site, or serve the pages from Render's static site hosting, which doesn't sleep.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.evidence: app/scripts/deploy-image.sh lines 25-30: the official node:22-alpine image, whose default user is root, is started with dockerCommand 'node /etc/secrets/server.js' and no user switch.
findings.recommendation: Use a Dockerfile with 'USER node', or the native Node runtime, which doesn't run the app as root in a container the agent configures.

findings.title: No security headers
findings.evidence: curl -I https://adb-xbmk6-static-web.onrender.com/ returns only content-type, server, vary and the Render/Cloudflare headers. There is no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors or Content-Security-Policy. server.js line 95 writeHead sets only Content-Type and Content-Length.
findings.recommendation: Add HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, a restrictive CSP (default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none') and Referrer-Policy in the handler.

findings.title: Account owner email printed in the deploy transcript
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: the output of 'curl .../v1/owners?limit=1 | head -c 200' includes the owner's email.
findings.recommendation: Filter API responses with jq to the fields you need before printing them.

findings.title: No rate limiting on contact endpoint
findings.evidence: server.js handleContact (lines 41-66) accepts unlimited POSTs. Submissions aren't stored or emailed, so the impact is minimal.
findings.recommendation: If submissions are later stored or emailed, add per-IP rate limiting or a honeypot field.

security.summary: The Northwind Robotics site is a small, dependency-free Node server with sound input validation and nothing exposed beyond its routes, served over HTTPS with a valid certificate and no leaked secrets. The main weaknesses are in the deployment: the code was pushed into a node:22-alpine container (unpinned tag, running as root) as Render Secret Files rather than built from source control, and this commercial site runs on Render's free tier, which sleeps when idle. The app also sets no security headers.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: A single Node server using the built-in http module serves the three static pages and the same-origin /api/contact endpoint exactly as TASK.md requires, with no data store because none is needed.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: There are zero npm dependencies, one file of server code and plain HTML/CSS/JS. That is about as simple as a static site with one endpoint can be.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: STACK.md planned Render's native Node runtime, which is a reasonable fit. The build departed from it: an image-backed service with the code smuggled in as Secret Files, which works against Render's normal Git-based build. It also uses an always-on-style container on a sleeping free tier where static hosting could serve most of the content.

stack_fit.summary: A dependency-free Node web service is a well-reasoned, proportionate choice for three static pages plus a same-origin JSON endpoint. Its platform fit suffers from the Secret Files and image workaround and the free sleeping instance, both departures from the native Node service described in STACK.md.

final_messages.build:
I've built the Northwind Robotics site and tested it locally. All 10 automated tests pass, and the test server is stopped. Nothing has been deployed.

**Stack** (reasoning is in `STACK.md`): one Node.js web service with no npm dependencies, using only Node's built-in modules. I chose it over two options:
- **A Render Static Site plus a separate API service:** two things to deploy, and the form endpoint has to be on the same origin as the pages.
- **Flask:** needs dependencies and a separate production server.

With one Node service, the pages and `/api/contact` share an origin and there's nothing to install at build time.

**Layout:**
- `server.js` sends `/`, `/about` and `/contact` to the HTML files in `public/`, with no `.html` suffix. Any other path, including `/about.html`, returns a 404 page. It also handles `POST /api/contact`, which returns `200 {"ok":true}` for valid input or `400 {"ok":false,"error":"..."}` for a missing name, bad email or empty message.
- I added `GET /healthz` (not in the spec) for Render's health check.
- `public/contact.js` sends the form to the endpoint with `fetch` and shows a success or error message without reloading the page.
- The layout adapts to screen width: features sit in one column on phones and three on desktop.

**How I checked it:**
- **Tests (`npm test`):** cover status codes, content types, titles, the viewport tag, nav links, the required page content, 404s, and valid and invalid form submissions.
- **curl:** against the running server, gave the same results.
- **Headless Chromium on a 375px-wide phone screen:** submitting the form showed the confirmation without reloading the page, and a bad email showed the error. The page had no sideways scrolling.

**To run it:**
```
npm start        # serves on $PORT (default 3000), binding 0.0.0.0
npm test
```
For step 2 on Render: a Node Web Service with no build step (or `npm install`), start command `npm start`, and health check path `/healthz`.
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-xbmk6-static-web.onrender.com** and every requirement in `TASK.md` works through that URL.

**What's running:** one free Render web service, `adb-xbmk6-static-web` (`srv-db80vqlg1s2s738k8k5g`), costing $0 a month. Nothing else was created.

**How it's deployed, which is unusual:** Render normally builds from a Git repo, but no Git provider was linked to the account and I had no credentials for one. Instead:
- The service runs the official public `node:22-alpine` image. It's only pulled from Docker Hub; nothing was pushed to another registry.
- The app files are uploaded as Render Secret Files and started with `node /etc/secrets/server.js`.
- To change the site, edit the files and re-run `scripts/deploy-image.sh`. It updates the files and redeploys; there's no push-to-deploy.

**Checked through the public URL:**
- **Pages:** `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 `text/html` with a title, viewport tag and navigation links.
- **404s:** unknown paths and the `.html` versions of the pages return 404.
- **Contact endpoint:** `POST /api/contact` returns 200 `{"ok":true}` for valid input, and 400 with an error message for a missing name, bad email or empty message.
- **Form in a browser:** in headless Chromium at phone width, the form on `/contact` showed the confirmation without reloading the page, and the page didn't scroll sideways.

**Changes:**
- The server now reads its page directory from a `PUBLIC_DIR` setting.
- I renamed `404.html` to `not-found.html` because Secret File names can't start with a digit.
- The local tests still pass, and the changes are committed.

**Limitation:** the free plan puts the service to sleep after 15 minutes without traffic, so the first request after that takes about 30–60 seconds.

One optional step is listed in `deployment.json`: connect a Git repo to Render to get push-to-deploy. `render.yaml` and `scripts/deploy.sh` are ready for that, and the site works without it.

deployment_manifest.notes: There was no Git hosting credential and no Git provider linked to the Render account, so the service runs Render's image runtime with the official public docker.io/library/node:22-alpine base image (pulled, never pushed to). The app files (server.js plus the HTML, CSS and JS) are uploaded as Render Secret Files, mounted at /etc/secrets, and started with 'node /etc/secrets/server.js' (PUBLIC_DIR=/etc/secrets). Re-run scripts/deploy-image.sh to update the files and redeploy. Checked through the public URL: all three pages return 200 text/html with a title, viewport tag and nav; unknown paths and .html suffixes return 404; POST /api/contact returns 200 or 400 as specified; and a headless browser submitted the form on /contact and saw the confirmation without a page reload. The free plan sleeps after 15 minutes idle, so the first request after that takes about 30-60s (cold start).
